plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to find the volume of the solid generated when the region under y = x^2 over [0, 2] is rotated about the line y = -1. The figure contains two linked views. Left (2D): the xy-plane showing the region R bounded above by the parabola y = x^2 and below by the x-axis between x = 0 and x = 2; the axis of revolution y = -1 is drawn as a horizontal red line, with a rotation arrow indicating revolution about it, and a representative washer cross-section at position x is sketched in gray. Right (3D): the resulting solid of revolution shown in perspective, with a visible central hole (from the inner radius of 1) and the parabolic outer surface. The figure illustrates the washer method: at each x, the cross-section is a washer with outer radius x^2 + 1 and inner radius 1, giving area pi((x^2 + 1)^2 - 1^2) = pi(x^4 + 2x^2), and the volume is computed by integrating this expression from 0 to 2.

elements: LEFT 2D panel: vertical y-axis with arrowhead and ticks at y=4 and y=x^2 (label positions), horizontal x-axis with arrowhead and ticks at x=0, x=2, and a moving tick at the slider position x
LEFT: blue generating curve y=f(x) drawn from x=0 to x=2 (default parabola x^2)
LEFT: light-blue shaded region R between the curve (top) and the x-axis y=0 (bottom) over [0,2], with vertical right edge at x=2 and label 'R' inside
LEFT: red horizontal axis-of-revolution line y=c (default y=-1) extending across the panel, labeled 'y = -1'
LEFT: curved rotation arrow around the red axis indicating revolution
LEFT: gray representative washer (annulus) drawn in slight 3D tilt at the slider x, centered on the red axis, outer radius f(x)-c, inner radius 0-c

RIGHT 3D panel: solid of revolution (trumpet/horn) with axis along world +X, narrow end at x=0 (left) flaring to wide end at x=2 (right); outer surface is the lathe of radius f(x)-c, light gray semi-transparent
RIGHT: central cylindrical hole of constant radius (0-c) running the full length, visible as the inner tube and as annular end faces
RIGHT: annular end cap (washer face) at x=2 (wide right end) and small annular cap at x=0
RIGHT: highlighted colored washer cross-section (annulus) at the slider x, matching the left representative washer
readout text: outer radius R(x)=f(x)-c, inner radius r=0-c, washer area A=pi(R^2-r^2) at the current x

interactions.label: Generating curve & axis
interactions.teaches: The function f(x) sets the outer edge of region R and the constant c sets the axis of revolution; together they fix every washer's outer radius f(x)-c and inner radius 0-c, so editing either reshapes the 2D region, the cross-section, and the 3D solid at once

interactions.label: Cross-section position x
interactions.teaches: Sweeping x moves the representative washer along the axis and live-updates outer radius, inner radius, and area pi(R^2-r^2), showing how the integrand of the washer method varies with x
Rotating the 3D solid reveals the central hole (inner radius) and the parabolic outer surface, confirming the cross-section is a washer (annulus), not a disk

demo_steps.title: Washer near the narrow end
demo_steps.narration: At x=0.5 the outer radius f(x)-c is small, so the washer is thin; the area pi(R^2-r^2) is small. The 3D horn is narrow here.

demo_steps.title: Washer at the midpoint
demo_steps.narration: At x=1 the outer radius is 1^2-(-1)=2 and inner radius 1, giving area pi(4-1)=3*pi. The highlighted annulus thickens.

demo_steps.title: Washer at the wide end
demo_steps.narration: At x=2 the outer radius is 2^2-(-1)=5 and inner radius 1, area pi(25-1)=24*pi — the largest washer, matching the flared right end of the solid.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Two linked sub-scenes sharing one camera. LEFT 2D plot lives in the world XY plane (facing +Z): map data x in [0,2] to world X in [-4,-1.5] and data y in [-1.5,4.5] to world Y in [-1.5,4.5] (1:1 vertical). Parabola as 120-pt THREE.Line blue #1a66cc; region R as filled ShapeGeometry light blue #cfe3f5 (top curve, bottom y=0, right edge x=2); axes black with arrowheads; red axis line y=c color #cc2222 spanning world X [-4.5,0.5]; rotation arrow a small torus-arc near X=-2.5 on the red line; representative washer an annulus (RingGeometry) tilted ~70 deg about X, gray #999999, centered on red line at the slider x. RIGHT 3D solid: axis along world +X from X=1.5 to X=4.5 (data x 0->2). World radius = (data radius)*0.35 so max outer radius (5) -> ~1.75 and inner radius (1) -> 0.35. Outer surface = LatheGeometry of profile radius f(x)-c; inner hole = open cylinder radius (0-c); end caps = annular RingGeometry at both ends; all light gray #cccccc opacity ~0.55. Highlighted washer = colored annulus #ff8800 at slider x on the solid. Readout panel shows R(x), r, A=pi(R^2-r^2). Default f=x^2, c=-1 over [0,2].
interactionPlan.notes: Rebuild the lathe profile, the 2D curve/region ShapeGeometry, both washers, and the readout reactively on every equation_input parse and on slider change; catch parse errors inline and keep the last valid geometry. Build the outer solid with THREE.LatheGeometry (segments ~64) and the inner hole as a separate open-ended CylinderGeometry so the central void reads correctly; render solids with DoubleSide and slight transparency so the hole and far surface are visible. Keep the left 2D panel unlit (MeshBasicMaterial) so it stays crisp and front-readable despite the perspective camera.

authoredContext: Find the volume of the solid generated when the region under the curve y = x2 over the interval [0, 2] is rotated about the line y =−1. Solution. First sketch the region and the axis of revolution; then imagine revolving the region about the axis (Figure 5.2.17). At each x in the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, the cross section of the solid perpendicular to the axis y =−1 is a washer with outer radius x2 + 1 and inner radius 1. Since the area of this washer is A(x) = π([x2 + 1] 2 − 12 ) = π(x4 + 2x2 ) it follows by (3) that the volume of the solid is V = ! 2 0 A(x) dx = ! 2 0 π x4 + 2x2_x000b_ dx = π 1 5 x5 + 2 3 x3 _x0010_2 0 = 176π 15

plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to find the volume of the solid generated when the region under y = x^2 over [0, 2] is rotated about the line y = -1. The figure contains two linked views. Left (2D): the xy-plane showing the region R bounded above by the parabola y = x^2 and below by the x-axis between x = 0 and x = 2; the axis of revolution y = -1 is drawn as a horizontal red line, with a rotation arrow indicating revolution about it, and a representative washer cross-section at position x is sketched in gray. Right (3D): the resulting solid of revolution shown in perspective, with a visible central hole (from the inner radius of 1) and the parabolic outer surface. The figure illustrates the washer method: at each x, the cross-section is a washer with outer radius x^2 + 1 and inner radius 1, giving area pi((x^2 + 1)^2 - 1^2) = pi(x^4 + 2x^2), and the volume is computed by integrating this expression from 0 to 2.

elements: LEFT 2D panel: vertical y-axis with arrowhead and ticks at y=4 and y=x^2 (label positions), horizontal x-axis with arrowhead and ticks at x=0, x=2, and a moving tick at the slider position x
LEFT: blue generating curve y=f(x) drawn from x=0 to x=2 (default parabola x^2)
LEFT: light-blue shaded region R between the curve (top) and the x-axis y=0 (bottom) over [0,2], with vertical right edge at x=2 and label 'R' inside
LEFT: red horizontal axis-of-revolution line y=c (default y=-1) extending across the panel, labeled 'y = -1'
LEFT: curved rotation arrow around the red axis indicating revolution
LEFT: gray representative washer (annulus) drawn in slight 3D tilt at the slider x, centered on the red axis, outer radius f(x)-c, inner radius 0-c

RIGHT 3D panel: solid of revolution (trumpet/horn) with axis along world +X, narrow end at x=0 (left) flaring to wide end at x=2 (right); outer surface is the lathe of radius f(x)-c, light gray semi-transparent
RIGHT: central cylindrical hole of constant radius (0-c) running the full length, visible as the inner tube and as annular end faces
RIGHT: annular end cap (washer face) at x=2 (wide right end) and small annular cap at x=0
RIGHT: highlighted colored washer cross-section (annulus) at the slider x, matching the left representative washer
readout text: outer radius R(x)=f(x)-c, inner radius r=0-c, washer area A=pi(R^2-r^2) at the current x

interactions.label: Generating curve & axis
interactions.teaches: The function f(x) sets the outer edge of region R and the constant c sets the axis of revolution; together they fix every washer's outer radius f(x)-c and inner radius 0-c, so editing either reshapes the 2D region, the cross-section, and the 3D solid at once

interactions.label: Cross-section position x
interactions.teaches: Sweeping x moves the representative washer along the axis and live-updates outer radius, inner radius, and area pi(R^2-r^2), showing how the integrand of the washer method varies with x
Rotating the 3D solid reveals the central hole (inner radius) and the parabolic outer surface, confirming the cross-section is a washer (annulus), not a disk

demo_steps.title: Washer near the narrow end
demo_steps.narration: At x=0.5 the outer radius f(x)-c is small, so the washer is thin; the area pi(R^2-r^2) is small. The 3D horn is narrow here.

demo_steps.title: Washer at the midpoint
demo_steps.narration: At x=1 the outer radius is 1^2-(-1)=2 and inner radius 1, giving area pi(4-1)=3*pi. The highlighted annulus thickens.

demo_steps.title: Washer at the wide end
demo_steps.narration: At x=2 the outer radius is 2^2-(-1)=5 and inner radius 1, area pi(25-1)=24*pi — the largest washer, matching the flared right end of the solid.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Two linked sub-scenes sharing one camera. LEFT 2D plot lives in the world XY plane (facing +Z): map data x in [0,2] to world X in [-4,-1.5] and data y in [-1.5,4.5] to world Y in [-1.5,4.5] (1:1 vertical). Parabola as 120-pt THREE.Line blue #1a66cc; region R as filled ShapeGeometry light blue #cfe3f5 (top curve, bottom y=0, right edge x=2); axes black with arrowheads; red axis line y=c color #cc2222 spanning world X [-4.5,0.5]; rotation arrow a small torus-arc near X=-2.5 on the red line; representative washer an annulus (RingGeometry) tilted ~70 deg about X, gray #999999, centered on red line at the slider x. RIGHT 3D solid: axis along world +X from X=1.5 to X=4.5 (data x 0->2). World radius = (data radius)*0.35 so max outer radius (5) -> ~1.75 and inner radius (1) -> 0.35. Outer surface = LatheGeometry of profile radius f(x)-c; inner hole = open cylinder radius (0-c); end caps = annular RingGeometry at both ends; all light gray #cccccc opacity ~0.55. Highlighted washer = colored annulus #ff8800 at slider x on the solid. Readout panel shows R(x), r, A=pi(R^2-r^2). Default f=x^2, c=-1 over [0,2].
interactionPlan.notes: Rebuild the lathe profile, the 2D curve/region ShapeGeometry, both washers, and the readout reactively on every equation_input parse and on slider change; catch parse errors inline and keep the last valid geometry. Build the outer solid with THREE.LatheGeometry (segments ~64) and the inner hole as a separate open-ended CylinderGeometry so the central void reads correctly; render solids with DoubleSide and slight transparency so the hole and far surface are visible. Keep the left 2D panel unlit (MeshBasicMaterial) so it stays crisp and front-readable despite the perspective camera.
